explanation: Complete transection above C5 results in quadriplegia due to interruption of all descending motor pathways to both upper and lower extremities; C3-C5 also affects phrenic nerve roots.
Hemisection produces ipsilateral proprioception loss (dorsal column) and UMN signs; A and B only captures these correctly; pain/temperature is contralateral.
In Brown-Sequard, LMN at same level is ipsilateral, not contralateral; this is the exception being tested among the listed features.
UMN lesion produces spastic paralysis, hyperreflexia, and Babinski positive (E); other options describe LMN or normal findings.
LMN lesion causes marked muscle wasting; hypertonia, absent/increased reflexes, and Babinski are UMN features not seen in LMN.
Syringomyelia first causes bilateral pain and temperature loss as the expanding syrinx damages crossing spinothalamic fibers.
Hindbrain comprises medulla, pons, cerebellum, and fourth ventricle; crus cerebri is a midbrain structure.
Brain stem = midbrain + pons + medulla; cerebellum and cerebral aqueduct are excluded from brain stem proper.
Cranial accessory nerve arises from nucleus ambiguus and joins vagus nerve; this explains its functional integration with CN X.
Spinal lemniscus carries contralateral pain and temperature sensation because spinothalamic fibers cross at their entry level.
Posterior spinal arteries and radicular arteries both supply dorsal columns; all of these sources contribute to dorsal column blood supply.
L4 spinous process is the landmark for lumbar puncture; needle inserted at L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace below the conus medullaris.
Complete section above C5 causes quadriplegia (all limbs); paraplegia requires thoracic lesion, hemiplegia requires cerebral lesion.
Hemisection produces ipsilateral proprioception loss and UMN signs; A and B only captures both correctly; pain loss is contralateral.
Brown-Sequard LMN at same level is ipsilateral, not contralateral; this makes D the exception.
UMN produces hyperreflexia, spasticity, and Babinski positive; normal plantar flexion (E) is not a UMN sign.
LMN lesion causes flaccid paralysis and marked muscle wasting; hypertonia, hyperreflexia, and Babinski are UMN signs.
Syringomyelia causes bilateral suspended sensory loss for pain/temperature; the central syrinx crosses pain fibers first.
Hindbrain = medulla + pons + cerebellum + fourth ventricle; crus cerebri is midbrain (mesencephalon).
Brain stem excludes cerebellum; cerebellum is a separate brain division connected via cerebellar peduncles.
Cranial XI from nucleus ambiguus joins vagus nerve; spinal part from C1-C5 is separate, explaining dual origin.
Spinal lemniscus carries contralateral pain and temperature after decussation at spinal levels.
Posterior spinal arteries (from vertebral) and radicular arteries supply dorsal columns; both contribute.
L4 spinous process is the anatomical landmark for lumbar puncture; needle inserted at L3-L4 or L4-L5.
Complete section above C5 causes quadriplegia; this is because all corticospinal fibers are interrupted before branching to limb motor pools.
Hemisection produces ipsilateral proprioception loss (dorsal column) and UMN signs; A and B only is correct.
Brown-Sequard shows ipsilateral LMN at same level; contralateral LMN would not occur from a hemisection.
